Sixty seconds on, thirty off, ten rounds.

That's fifteen minutes and it's harder than most people's hour. Intervals work because the rest is what lets you actually push during the work.

Rope, watch, done before your coffee gets cold.

The plan you follow beats the perfect plan.

There is no optimal program. There's the one you'll actually do on a Tuesday in November when it's dark and you're tired.

Pick the boring one you can repeat and stop redesigning it.

#fitnessmotivation #consistency #training #fitnesstips #discipline

Do your cardio first thing in the morning.

Not because it burns more — because it's done before the day gets a vote. Nothing gets scheduled over it, nothing runs late, and you spend the rest of the day already having won something.

I do mine before I lift. It changes how the whole day feels.

Drink more water than feels necessary.

It blunts appetite, it improves training output, and it stops the mild dehydration that most people read as tiredness at 3pm.

It's the least interesting advice in fitness and one of the few that works for everyone.

Abs are made in the kitchen, and here's the actual number.

Visible abs for most men means getting body fat somewhere in the low teens. There's no ab exercise that does that — it's a kitchen result you reveal.

Know the number you're aiming at and the plan writes itself.

Hire a cleaner instead of a personal trainer.

A trainer at $200 a month teaches you things AI will now tell you for free. Two hours a week of your life back is worth more than someone counting your reps.

Buy time, not supervision.
